targets.title: Forward audit — Erdős #944 candidate order lower bound
targets.prompt:
Independently audit the following frozen candidate lemma arising during work on Erdős problem #944. This is only a necessary condition and must never be presented as solving the open existence problem.

Exact setting: let G be a finite simple graph with chromatic number 4; assume chi(G-v)=3 for every vertex v and chi(G-e)=4 for every edge e. Frozen claim: |V(G)| >= 11.

Frozen proof candidate. For each v and every proper 3-coloring phi of G-v, every color must occur at least twice in N_G(v): absence of a color would extend phi to G, while exactly one occurrence at a neighbor w would extend phi to G-vw, contradicting chi(G-vw)=4. Hence delta(G)>=6. Put H=complement(G), and let theta(H) be the minimum number of cliques partitioning V(H). Then theta(H)=4, theta(H-v)=3 for all v, and Delta(H)<=n-7 where n=|V(H)|. Orders n<=7 are immediate. For n=8, Delta(H)<=1 and theta(H)=4 forces H to be a perfect matching, but theta(H-v)=4. For n=9, Delta(H)<=2; every 3-clique partition of H-v has sizes 3,3,2, and each triangle is a component of H. Fixing v produces triangle components, and deleting a vertex of one such component forces two further disjoint triangle components, so H=3K3 and theta(H)=3, contradiction. For n=10, Delta(H)<=3. H cannot contain K4: any K4 is a component, and deleting one of its vertices leaves clique-partition number 4. Every H-v therefore has a partition into three triangles. Fix u. A factor after deleting some vertex not u puts u in a triangle, so choose a neighbor a. The factor of H-a puts u in a triangle with two further neighbors b,c. Thus d_H(u)=3 and N_H(u)={a,b,c}. Factors of H-a, H-b, and H-c force respectively bc, ac, and ab, so {u,a,b,c} induces K4, contradiction.

Audit obligations: freeze this exact statement and proof; try to falsify every step and every endpoint n=8,9,10; check the color-multiplicity equivalence, complement translation, clique-partition additivity, and all component claims. If useful, perform an independent exhaustive finite graph/certificate check, but declare its exact scope. Distinguish a valid lower bound from novelty and from existence. Preserve any correction as an explicit finding. Even if the lemma is accepted, the outcome relative to Erdős #944 is Partial Progress, never Solved or Counterexample. Source context: https://www.erdosproblems.com/944.

audit_suffix: CANDIDATE AUDIT GATE: Work with the selected harness and model only. Read `_agent/skills/research-proof-audit/SKILL.md` completely and follow the relevant references before finalizing. Freeze the exact lemma and candidate, run independent global and decomposed audits, add a refuter/boundary pass, and preserve disagreements and failed checks. A file-capable harness MUST write and validate global.json, decomposed.json, verifier-output.json, merge-map.json, and nonempty run.json under one `audit/<run-id>/` directory. If the contract cannot be completed, explicitly state `degraded audit:` and list every missing or invalid artifact. End proof.md with exactly `ProvingConsole outcome: Partial Progress`. An audit accept verdict establishes at most this reusable lemma, not Erdős #944 and not novelty.
baseline_suffix: CONTROL CONDITION: Audit the frozen lemma rigorously without invoking the research-proof-audit skill. Preserve reproducible evidence, do not infer novelty or existence, and end proof.md with exactly `ProvingConsole outcome: Partial Progress`.
